Bill.BriefDescription: Modifying the income thresholds for the exemption and deferral property tax relief programs for senior citizens and persons retired because of physical disability.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to modifying the income thresholds for theexemption and deferral property tax relief programs for senior citizensand persons retired because of physical disability; and creating a newsection.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The legislature recognizes that propertytaxes impose a substantial financial burden on those with fixedincomes. The legislature further recognizes that property tax reliefprograms have considerable value in addressing this burden. However,the legislature also recognizes that property tax relief programs usestatic income thresholds that must be updated periodically to reflectthe impact of inflation, and these thresholds do not reflect disparateincome levels across the state. The legislature further recognizesthat the definition of disposable income may not accurately reflect anindividual's ability to pay property taxes. The legislature furtherrecognizes that the assessed value limits in these programs do notreflect the substantial disparity in property values across the state.Therefore, the legislature recognizes that policy questions arise as tothe appropriate thresholds and limits to use as part of the senior p. 1 SHB 1170citizens, disabled persons, and veterans property tax relief programs,the timing and manner of adjustments to those thresholds and limits,and whether these programs should be modified in other substantive waysto better reflect their intended purpose. (2)(a) Therefore, it is the legislature's intent to have thedepartment of revenue study the issues outlined in subsection (1) ofthis section relating to the senior citizens, disabled persons, andveterans property tax relief programs in RCW 84.36.381, et seq. andchapter 84.38 RCW, with input from the members of a task force. Thetask force is comprised of four members: (i) One person employed withthe department of revenue; (ii) one person from an associationrepresenting county assessors; (iii) one person from an associationrepresenting persons retired by reason of age; and (iv) one person froman association representing veterans retired by reason of disability.The department of revenue must appoint the task force members.Legislative fiscal staff may provide technical assistance to the taskforce. (b) The task force must choose its chair from among its membership. (3) The task force review must include an analysis of thefollowing: (a) Assessed property values by county, including per capitaamounts; (b) Median income by county; (c) The revenue impact of the programs on the state and localtaxing districts and taxpayers, including property tax shifts; (d) Changes in the average life expectancy and retirement age sincethe inception of the programs; (e) Changes in the amount of state and local property taxes paid asa percentage of personal income since the inception of the programs; (f) The passage of additional property tax relief programs that maybe available to senior citizens and persons retired by reason ofdisability; (g) Any other data the task force deems necessary to properlyevaluate and make recommendation on the property tax relief programsfor senior citizens and persons retired by reason of disability. (4) By December 1, 2013, and in compliance with RCW 43.01.036, thedepartment of revenue must submit a report to the appropriate fiscal SHB 1170 p. 2 committees of the legislature that details the department's findingsand recommendations.
